notes: controlSpreadPct is the largest difference between the medians of two identical runs (tree vs tree) over all 38 (mix, n) cells, for the two scenarios. controlSpread has the median and the largest difference of each metric. Treat two formats closer than about twice this as the same.

Scenario firstLoad: one fresh headless Chromium process per measurement, CPU throttled 4x. `load` is JSON.parse of the catalog text, or evaluating the script for the Paraglide formats (which includes their runtime chunk). `render` is setting the library up and formatting the first 100 messages of the catalog once (all of them when n is smaller). `total` is load + render. `evalRuntime` is evaluating the library's script; it is reported apart and is not in `total`. Not timed: fetching the files.

Scenario serverRender: one fresh Node process per measurement. After the timed parse, first render and re-render of the whole catalog, it formats the whole catalog over and over for 100 ms without timing, then for 100 ms more: messagesPerMs is messages formatted per millisecond in that second window.

ms.parse, ms.firstRender and ms.reRender are single calls for the whole catalog in that Node process, in this order, after one gc(): parse and firstRender run with cold JIT. For the Paraglide formats parse is evaluating the script.

Intl is warmed before the timed section in both scenarios (one Intl.PluralRules, two Intl.NumberFormat, one Intl.DateTimeFormat are built and used, untimed), so the numbers are the library's own work. The Intl floor, in a fresh process with no message library: Node, PluralRules + NumberFormat 6.783 ms (min 6.565, max 7.136), plus a percent NumberFormat and a DateTimeFormat 8.807 ms (min 8.561, max 9.633) in total; Chromium at 4x, 18.11 ms (min 17.49, max 34.93) and 21.48 ms (min 20.59, max 42.49). A process pays this once, whatever the format.

bytes: the catalog JSON `{16-hex key: value}`; gzip level 6; brotli quality 11; valuesGzip is gzip of the JSON array of values without keys. icu and icu-fjs read the same catalog. Sizes do not change on a rerun with the same Node version; gzip sizes differ slightly between zlib versions.
runtimeBytes: the one import that formats, bundled and minified for the browser (esbuild; Vite for Paraglide and Intlayer, which need their own plugins); gzip level 6, brotli quality 11.

locales: how many locales the app has. Each locale has the same messages, with the letters of the text substituted, so every locale has the same size. A format with `localeInvariant` ships one file per locale: what a user downloads does not depend on the locale count, and its cells are at locales = 1.

fits: metric = fixed + perMessage * n for each (format, mix, locales), by least squares on the relative error; maxErrorPct is the worst relative error of the line. downloadGzipBytes is bytes.gzip + runtimeBytes.gzip over all sizes; firstLoadMs is the firstLoad total over the sizes from one page up.

Corpus is synthetic (seeded). Every format printed the same string for all 10000 messages of both mixes before timing, except Intlayer as its note says. See README for what was left out and what favours or hurts each format.

formats.label: ICU string, gt formatIcu
formats.note: Parses the string on every call: gt keeps no parsed-message cache, so a re-render parses again.

formats.label: ICU string, intl-messageformat
formats.note: Parses once per key; the IntlMessageFormat object is cached per key. With react-intl's formatter cache (@formatjs/intl createFormatters) the bundle is 34899 min / 10173 gzip / 9051 brotli.

formats.label: FormatJS precompiled AST
formats.runtime: intl-messageformat IntlMessageFormat given the AST of `formatjs compile --ast`
formats.note: runtimeBytes is with @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser aliased to its no-parser.js. Without that alias the parser stays in the bundle: 33720 min / 9926 gzip / 8848 brotli.

formats.label: Lingui compiled message
formats.note: Plain text is stored as a one-element array. Formats on each call; nothing is cached per key.

formats.label: next-intl icu-minify
formats.note: runtimeBytes is icu-minify/format alone. It needs the caller's formatter cache and named-style table; with next-intl's (use-intl format-only wrapper + formatter cache) the bundle is 4344 min / 1689 gzip / 1527 brotli.

formats.label: gt message tree
formats.note: The catalog holds the tree alone. Formatting context (`formats`) is empty for every message of this corpus.

formats.label: Paraglide JS compiled functions
formats.runtime: the message functions that @inlang/paraglide-js compiles (Vite plugin, default options)
formats.note: Not a catalog: one JavaScript function per message, produced from the ICU strings by @inlang/plugin-icu1 and bundled by Vite with paraglideVitePlugin. `bytes` is the chunk of message functions and holds no keys, because an app calls each function by name and the bundler drops the names; compare it with `valuesGzip` of the catalogs. Each function holds the text of every locale, so `bytes` grows with the locale count. `runtimeBytes` is the chunk the functions import (locale detection and Intl helpers) and is per cell.

formats.label: Paraglide JS, per-locale build
formats.runtime: the same functions, built for one locale (experimentalPerLocaleBuild)
formats.note: The `en` bundle of experimentalPerLocaleBuild (Vite 8, Rolldown): the other locales and the locale detection are compiled out. The build checks that it is the same file for 1, 5 and 20 locales.

formats.label: Intlayer dictionary
formats.runtime: @intlayer/core getDictionary and its ICU message resolver (static import mode)
formats.note: One dictionary of n fields, built from the ICU JSON files by @intlayer/sync-json-plugin (format: 'icu'), with every locale in it (import mode 'static', the default), so `bytes` grows with the locale count. Formatted the way @intlayer/react-intl formats: getDictionary, then the ICU resolver, which still parses a plain-text message as ICU on each call. Not the same output as ICU: `#` prints without grouping (1234, not 1,234) and a select on a variable not named `value` takes its fallback branch. Messages that differ, of 10000: app {"plural":21}, rich {"selectPlural":501,"plural":750,"select":990}. `runtimeBytes` is built by vite-intlayer, which drops the node types a project does not use, and is per cell.

formats.label: Intlayer dictionary, dynamic import mode
formats.runtime: the same calls on the per-locale dictionary
formats.note: The dictionary of one locale (import mode 'dynamic'). It lists the id of every locale's source file, about 80 bytes per locale, so it is measured for each locale count.
